title: a wb write that lands can report failure on a locked store, and neither lock report says whether the write landed
body:
A whiteboard write can land and then report failure when the store is locked, and the report does not say whether the write landed. That is the inverse of No Silent Errors: the write is silent and the error is false. The caller's only way to learn the truth is to read the board back.

Observed on this tree at 2026-09-14 12:09Z (ic). The command was run just after dc's 4c172d260 build was promoted, while dc's post-promotion `intent doctor` and the new intentd's first ingest were open on the store:

```
intent wb archive doing 19 --node ic
```

It exited rc 1 with:

```
error: could not read the committed canon
  caused by: sqlite: database is locked
  caused by: database is locked
  caused by: Error code 5: The database file is locked
  remedy: fix the artefacts named above, then retry -- run `intent doctor` to list them
```

The archive had landed. The same command, re-issued, answered `ok: ic has no live doing 19` at rc 0, and `intent wb show ic --json` showed doing 19 archived. `Facade::wb_archive` commits the store write (`wb_archive_item`, mapped to `FacadeError::Store`) and then calls `land_board_write`, and the `FacadeError::Ingest` it returned came from that second step. So the verb reports the post-write step's failure as the write's failure. The remedy then sends the caller to re-issue a write that has already happened.

A sibling shape, met by vc the same morning: `intent wb add doing` refused with `could not update the runtime store: database is locked` and did NOT land: that is `FacadeError::Store`, the write's own step. So one lock has two outcomes, landed and not landed, and neither report says which one happened. A caller that retries on the first shape double-applies any write that is not idempotent (`wb add`, `wb ask`, `wb decide` each append a new row).

Two more instances the same hour, each widening the family. Filing this issue hit the same lock: `intent issues add` refused with `could not update the runtime store` and the remedy `the change was not made`, and it had appended its `ISSUE:<n>` row to `intent/.intentfiles` with no store row, canon or view behind it. So a "not made" report can also leave a partial write on disk. Nothing else wrote it: the only diff in that file was the one row, restored by hand before the retry. And dc met the double-apply at d6ffb6fd0: a `wb add` that stored its row and then failed on a locked store, whose retry left a duplicate item that had to be archived by hand.

What the fix has to give the caller, none of it ruled:
- A failure after the store commit reports that the write landed and names only the step that failed (eg the canon or view refresh), with a remedy that is not "retry".
- A failure before the commit keeps saying the write did not happen. It also leaves nothing behind: no register row in `intent/.intentfiles` without the store row it names.
